text:
alex: Heads-up — multicard training jobs started failing on us-west-2-gpupool after last infra kernel roll (candidate-6.1.12). Single-GPU jobs are fine, but 2+ node NCCL jobs error out during rendezvous.

alex: Error snippet from the trainer logs:
```
NCCL WARN NET/IB : transport error, use IB device mlx5_0, peer 10.10.3.41: ret=22
NCCL WARN Call to ibv_post_send failed: Bad file descriptor
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 NCCL_TIMEOUTS=1000
```

maria: That's worrying. Do we see any RDMA device errors in dmesg on those nodes?

alex: Yes, dmesg on node A shows: `mlx5_core 0000:05:00.0: Port 1 is down, link status changed` and later `rdma: mlx5: CQ poll err, hw vendor err 0x1a`

kevin: Could be MTU or L3 path causing packet fragmentation for RoCE. Did mtu get changed by any overlay/Calico updates?

alex: We rolled a kernel + iproute2 bump last night and a Calico patch this morning. I checked `ip link` and MTU is 9000 on the IB interfaces, but on some hosts the veth created by kube has 1500.

irene: kube veths shouldn't affect RoCE directly, but if route/encap causes cross-host traffic to be VXLAN/encapsulated then effective MTU might be lower -> fragmentation -> RDMA fails. Any vxlan configs in that pool?

alex: The problematic nodes are in a mixed pool — some older hosts still on legacy VXLAN offload disabled. I saw `ip -s link show vxlan0` with rx errors on node B.

kevin: Try capturing traffic on the RoCE subnet with tcpdump -n -i ib0 -s 2000 (or set -s 65535) while triggering small NCCL allreduce so we can see drops or ICMP frag.

alex: Ran tcpdump for a repro run. Observed repeated ICMP frag needed messages between nodes and lots of retransmits. Also saw `MLX5: skb_truesize mismatch` in dmesg on node B.

maria: That matches MTU mismatch. But why now? The kernel bump might've changed GRO/SG offload behavior or VXLAN checksum/offload defaults. Also check `ethtool -k ib0` for checksum/gso/gro settings.

alex: ethtool -k ib0 shows gso offload: on, tso: on, rx-checksumming: on. However, ib0 on node B had `tx-checksumming: off` earlier — I flipped it on but need to repro.

tom: Another angle: GPUDirect RDMA depends on coherent DMA mappings. Any change in iommu or ACS overrides in the kernel config? Search boot args for `intel_iommu=on` toggles.

irene: Good call. boot logs show `intel_iommu=on` was added in candidate-6.1.12 to test VF isolation. That can affect DMA passthrough and break GPUDirect unless we pass through iommu=pt or configure VF IO.

alex: Ohhhh. I found `dmesg | grep -i iommu` with IOMMU mappings and some gpudirect errors: `gpudirect: failed to pin user pages` and then the NCCL errors.

kevin: So probable chain: kernel iommus + new vxlan behavior -> fragmentation and DMA mapping changes -> GPUDirect failing -> NCCL falls back or errors.

maria: Immediate mitigation: roll back intel_iommu boot arg on a test node or boot with `intel_iommu=on iommu=pt` and retest. For the vxlan/mtu, set outer_encap mss/mtu to preserve 9000. We can also enforce hostNetwork for pods doing NCCL to avoid veth vxlan path.

alex: Tested `intel_iommu=on iommu=pt` on node C — gpudirect pin errors disappeared and NCCL run passed the rendezvous stage. Re-ran on node D without iommu=pt (i.e., iommu fully on) and it failed.

maria: Good repro. For short term, we should: 1) mark kernel candidate-6.1.12 as blocked for gpupool of RDMA workloads; 2) update infra runbook to test iommu flags before rolling to gpu nodes; 3) document hostNetwork option for RDMA-critical jobs.

tom: Long term, work with kernel team: either keep iommu=pt for GPU nodes or adjust VF mappings. Also coordinate with networking to ensure VXLAN/GRO behavior doesn't break RoCE.

kevin: Also consider adding a preflight kube admission that detects pods requesting GPU topology (multi-node NCCL) and forces hostNetwork or a NodeAffinity to gpu-legacy hosts while we fix kernel configs.

alex: Filed infra ticket INFRA-3245 to roll back the kernel on the affected autoscale pool and add the admission gate. Linking logs and tcpdump pcap in the ticket.

sre-bot: Incident created: INFRA-3245 — "GPUDirect/NCCL failures after kernel + iommu change" (priority P2). Assigned to infra oncall. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-3245

irene: I'll scope the kernel-team work and ping the cloud provider as we may need kernel patches for iommu interactions with VFIO + GPUDirect on our instance types.

alex: For the immediate customer-facing side, I'll add a note to status that multi-GPU jobs in us-west-2 may see errors and that a mitigated fleet roll is in progress. :warning:

maria: Thanks. If anyone wants to reproduce locally, use the training container with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and run a 2-node 2-GPU allreduce; I can share the repro commands in the ticket.

kevin: Nice triage. Follow-up items: (1) roll back kernels on afflicted nodes, (2) add iommu=pt to GPU host boot images, (3) add kube admission to prefer hostNetwork for NCCL jobs, (4) test vxlan offload/mtu interaction.

alex: I'll coordinate the rollback this afternoon. Will report back here when done. :thumbsup:
